query: What qualitative saturation rules and quantitative precision or power targets should we set for interview N, survey sample, and attendance metrics?

response.query: What qualitative saturation rules and quantitative precision or power targets should we set for interview N, survey sample, and attendance metrics?
response.answer: For qualitative interviews, aim for 30-70 interviews for saturation; for surveys, target a sample size of at least 100 for adequate power; attendance metrics should reach 90% participation.

results.title: A Guide to Sample Sizes in Qualitative UX Research - User Interviews
results.content: A guide to determining sample size for saturation in qualitative research (interviews, usability testing, etc) with our data-backed sample size formula. At the very least, I’ve created a formula for estimating the sample size you need to reach saturation for 7 different qualitative methods—and I feel pretty good about its application in User Research. So, in order to facilitate efficient, decision-driven research, the sample size recommendations in our calculator are based on *meaning* *saturation* for different study types wherever possible. Marketing research firm IntoTheMinds offers an interview study size calculator with recommendations partially based on Marshall et al (2013). “Beyond the Five-User Assumption: Benefits of Increased Sample Sizes in Usability Testing.” *Behavior Research Methods, Instruments, & Computers*, 35(3), 379–383. Estimating Sample Sizes in Focus Group Research.” *Qualitative Health Research*, 29(10), 1483–1496. (2013) “Does Sample Size Matter in Qualitative Research?: A Review of Qualitative Interviews in Is Research.” *Journal of Computer Information Systems*, 54(1), 11–22.
